subject: Mutual action plan & production readiness: POC env gating
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <s.lee@mediq.com>, Tom Baxter <t.baxter@mediq.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual action plan & production readiness: POC env gating

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks for the call earlier. Per our discussion I’ve attached an initial mutual action plan (MAP-MediQ-v2.xlsx) that lays out the minimal gating items to get your POC running on Redwood: API key provisioning, org + tenant setup, IP allowlist for our hosted endpoints, and optional VPC peering for private traffic.

High-level proposed cadence (target close window: 2 weeks):
- Day 0: Sign MAP / procurement acknowledgement (procurement@mediq.com)
- Day 1: Redwood issues API key(s) scoped to the POC tenant
- Day 1-2: MedIQ completes org setup and service account mapping
- Day 2-3: IP allowlist (we’ll need the CIDRs) — this unlocks immediate hosted testing
- Day 3-7: VPC peering request + peering validation (optional for initial tests; required if you want private egress)

Action items for MedIQ to confirm:
1) Primary POC contact for networking (name + email)
2) CIDR ranges for IP allowlist (or we can provide a whitelist if you prefer to accept ours)
3) Procurement timeline (DocuSign or PO) so we can align billing and resource reservations

Attachments: MAP-MediQ-v2.xlsx (mutual action plan) — please review the ownership column. I’ve left the VPC peering step optional in the MAP; if you want peering parallel to API key work we can shift resources.

If it helps I can schedule a 30-min tech sync with Ben to walk your network team through the peering checklist.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this on a short runway.

—
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MAP-MediQ-v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

Thanks Priyom — this looks good and aligns with what Tom and I discussed. A couple quick clarifications before we sign: 

- Procurement: We typically need a brief SOW + PO; procurement@mediq.com will pick up the MAP once we have the cost line items. Can you send a one-page SOW?
- IP allowlist: attaching our CIDR export for the staging VPC. (See mediq-ip-allowlist.csv)
- VPC peering: our infra team prefers a cross-account peering (no shared VPC) and will need your AWS account IDs and the peering template. Is there a template you use? Also: do you support route propagation or prefer static routes?

We’ll make the network contact available — Sara Kim (sara.kim@mediq.com, infra lead) — she can join the tech sync. We aim to have procurement sign-off within 5 business days once we have the SOW.

Happy to sign the MAP once those two items are in place.

Best,
Samantha
Director, Product — MedIQ Health
[Attachment: mediq-ip-allowlist.csv (text/csv)]

Looping in the engineering perspective — thanks for the MAP, Priyom. Quick notes from a peering / network gating angle: 

- AWS account IDs: we’ll send a short peering template (account IDs + VPC IDs + region). Priyom, I’ll add the template to the drive link once I have your go-ahead.
- CIDR overlap: we must ensure MedIQ CIDRs do not overlap with Redwood-hosted tenant ranges. I scanned mediq-ip-allowlist.csv and flagged a potential 10.0.0.0/16 overlap if you intend to use that block; can you confirm which ranges are actually used in the staging environment?
- Route propagation vs static routes: recommendation = static routes on both sides for predictable traffic flows during the POC. If you want dynamic propagation we can enable it but will plan extra verification.
- NAT/egress: if you plan to access external services from the peered VPC you may need to account for SNAT rules; redwood's hosted endpoints expect source IPs on the allowlist for token-bound rate limiting.

Timeline suggestion (technical):
- T0: API key issuance (hosted testing) — this should be same-day once we have the signed MAP and SOW
- T0-T1: IP allowlist validation (we can test connectivity with a curl to our /health endpoint)
- T2-T4: VPC peering request + route validation (allow 48–72 hours for route table changes & verification)

I attached a short peering checklist that we use with customers to avoid common delays.

—Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: vpc-peering-draft.pdf (application/pdf)]

Appreciate the quick turnaround. To keep momentum I’ve summarized the agreed next steps and owners below. If you confirm, we’ll consider the MAP accepted and proceed to issue keys and open the tech workstreams.

Confirmed next steps:
- Procurement: Redwood to send a 1‑page SOW and the cost table by EOD Monday — owner: Priyom (priyom_das@redwood.com).
- Networking: Sara Kim (sara.kim@mediq.com) to validate the mediq-ip-allowlist.csv and confirm final CIDRs — owner: MedIQ infra.
- API keys + tenant: Redwood will generate scoped API key(s) for the POC tenant once MAP + SOW are acknowledged — owner: Redwood infra (Ben).
- VPC peering: optional for initial tests. If MedIQ signs up for peering now, Ben will send the peering template and we’ll run the checklist during the T2-T4 window.
- Tech sync: 30-min session to walk Sara through the peering template and allowlist verification. Proposed slots: Tue 08/01 10:00–10:30 PT or Wed 08/02 14:00–14:30 PT — please confirm which works.

Please reply with acceptance of the MAP and which tech sync slot you prefer. Once you confirm I’ll mark action items in the MAP (owner column) and we’ll hand-off to engineering.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
